claims.text: Conventionally arc-melted MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration alloys have a relatively coarse grain structure.
Conventionally arc-melted MnNiSi-based alloys are brittle.
The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy exhibits a strong magnetocaloric effect near its transition.
High-pressure torsion followed by low-temperature annealing will refine and homogenize the grain structure of MnNiSi-based alloys.
Annealing at approximately 300°C for about one hour will restore crystallinity after severe plastic deformation.
The proposed annealing treatment will preserve a refined nanostructured grain size.
The treatment may produce strain-induced nanoscale precipitation.
Grain refinement will improve the balance of yield strength and ductility through a Hall–Petch mechanism.
The treatment will maintain the integrity of the magnetocaloric phase.
Integrity of the magnetocaloric phase is necessary for a large entropy change during the magnetostructural transition.
The processed material will exhibit significantly greater ductility than the untreated cast material.
The processed material will exhibit significantly greater toughness than the untreated cast material.
The processed material will retain a large magnetocaloric effect with only a minimal reduction in magnetic entropy change.
The processed material will show only a minimal change in transition temperature.
Excessive annealing-induced grain growth or recovery could eliminate the mechanical benefits of severe plastic deformation.
Excessively severe deformation or over-annealing could shift the magnetocaloric properties unfavorably.
